messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple healthcheck failures observed in eu-west-1 ELBs and elevated Route53 re-route activity. Errors and latency affecting hosted API endpoints. Pager -> @sre-oncall. Alert link: https://alerts.redwood/4387654321
alex: seeing the same on dashboards — spike in 5xx from services behind eu-west-1 ALBs. Confirming which stacks impacted.
maria: customers reporting widespread 502s for EU-hosted API endpoints. Error rate ~22% on our latency dashboard. CS triage picking up tickets.
cheng: I can take L2. Starting incident bridge and running runbook. Bridge: https://meet.redwood/bridges/INC-4387654321
sre-oncall: handing off to cheng for L2. I started runbook `aws-eu-network-dns-rewrite` steps 1-3. ELB target health is flapping, many targets becoming Unhealthy intermittently.
alex: logs show ELB healthchecks returning 503/504 intermittently; EBS iowait looks high on a subset of instances (i-0abcd1234). Could be underlying storage issue causing target failures.
lina: Route53 weighted routing is oscillating due to low TTLs (30s). Clients may be bouncing between regions while we try to remediate.
maria: Impact summary for ops: priority customers affected include AcmeLtd and Scriptly. High error volumes for EU customers. CS is notifying impacted accounts.
cheng: mitigation plan: 1) shift critical traffic from eu-west-1 to eu-central-1 via weighted Route53 update (temporary) 2) drain and replace unhealthy instances in eu-west-1 3) monitor ELB health and EBS metrics. @kevin can you perform the DNS weight change?
kevin: on it. Preparing Route53 change batch. Command I'll run: ```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123456 --change-batch file://change-weight.json``` will post change-id in ~20s.
incident-bot: Route53 change submitted by kevin. change-id: C1234567890. Status: PENDING
sre-oncall: initiated drain on unhealthy targetgroup in eu-west-1 and started extra warm hosts in eu-central-1. Autoscaling launched +4 instances in eu-central-1.
alex: EC2 console shows EBS latency spike on vol-0efgh5678 attached to i-0abcd1234. Marking instance for replacement.
lina: we should snapshot volumes prior to detach: `aws ec2 create-snapshot --volume-id vol-0efgh5678` then detach and reprovision on healthy host.
maria: CS update: ticket volume reduced slightly after DNS plan announced, but customers pinned to eu-west via cached entries still see errors.
product-ops: Suggesting status page draft: "We are experiencing elevated errors for EU-hosted APIs. Traffic is being shifted to a secondary region while we investigate." Approve to post?
kevin: Route53 change moved weights -> eu-central-1 80%, eu-west-1 20%. Change status now: INSYNC. Traffic shift progressing.
alex: telemetry improving — 5xx now down from 22% to ~3% after majority of traffic hit eu-central-1. Some intermittent 502s remain for cached clients.
sre-oncall: replacing two problematic EBS-backed instances now. Snapshotting volumes and provisioning replacements. Commands used: ```aws ec2 create-snapshot --volume-id vol-0efgh5678``` and ```aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids i-0abcd1234```
maria: CS escalation: offering temporary region reroute options and account credits to top impacted customers (AcmeLtd, Scriptly). Sales looped in.
cheng: next steps for RCA and cleanup: - verify EBS health + IO metrics across the cluster - review ELB healthcheck thresholds and backoff - tune Route53 failover runbook to handle low TTL oscillation - coordinate controlled shift-back when eu-west healthy
incident-bot: Incident severity updated -> SEV2. Owner -> cheng. Bridge pinned: https://meet.redwood/bridges/INC-4387654321
lina: plan for shift-back: incrementally reduce eu-central weight by 10% every 5 minutes once we confirm eu-west target stability for 10 minutes.
kevin: confirmations: all replacement instances report healthy in target groups. ELB health stable on new hosts. Ready to coordinate shift-back per lina's plan.
product-ops: posting status update to status.redwood.ai and sending customer email template. Noting affected regions and mitigation actions.
alex: assigning follow-ups: SRE -> check for any hardware-level EBS faults + open AWS support case if needed; Eng -> proxy abort threshold review; Product -> customer comms for top 10 accounts.
maria: CS: continuing to monitor tickets, keeping prioritized customers in the loop.
cheng: moving incident to monitoring mode. We'll keep this channel open for the postmortem and final RCA notes. Great work, team — closing active pages for now.
